script.text: Anthropic wants up to sixty-four billion dollars from one stock sale. Who is buying?

Anthropic, the company behind the Claude A.I. models, set the price range for its stock market debut on Tuesday. Its updated filing offers eight hundred twenty-five million shares at seventy to seventy-eight dollars each, to be listed on Nasdaq.

At the top of the range, that would raise about sixty-four billion dollars, TechCrunch and CNBC report. Counting all shares, it would value the company at up to one point four trillion dollars. Saudi Aramco raised about twenty-nine billion in twenty nineteen.

Seven tech giants, including Nvidia, Google and Microsoft, agreed to buy another twenty-six billion dollars of stock privately, the filing shows. Anthropic reported about seventeen billion dollars in third-quarter revenue. Sources told CNBC that trading could begin on November nineteenth.
Will Anthropic's shares start trading on November nineteenth? Yes or no?

upload.title: Anthropic's IPO Could Raise $64 Billion #shorts
upload.description:
A.I. company Anthropic set a price range of $70 to $78 per share for 825 million shares in its planned Nasdaq IPO on November 10, according to its amended SEC filing. At the top of the range that is about $64 billion in gross proceeds and an implied fully diluted valuation of up to about $1.4 trillion, per TechCrunch and CNBC. Seven companies including Nvidia, Google and Microsoft agreed to buy $26 billion of shares in a private placement; pricing and trading dates (Nov 18/19) come from people familiar with the matter cited by CNBC and are not final. Nothing here is investment advice.

Sources: Anthropic S-1/A (SEC), CNBC, TechCrunch, Decrypt, FourWeekMBA, The Tribune. Aramco 2019 figure: widely reported total including over-allotment.
